# Rendering

spec

One universal renderer produces a page per visible document at the path of its source: `docs/src/a/b.json` becomes `docs/out/a/b.md`. Pages start with a comment saying they are generated.

The title is the first level heading. Under it comes one line with the kind, status, priority and tags separated by a middle dot, then the body without a heading of its own, then the free fields in file order, each as a second level section named after the field. At the end of the page come the sections Parent, Referenced by (documents that point here through `parent` or through references outside `notes`) and Covered by (the paths of code files with a `docc:` tag, without line numbers). There is no separate section of links: the references stay in the text.

A reference to a document becomes a relative link whose text is the title of the target; a reference to a field or to a section inside a field links to its heading. A field made of sections is a second level heading with third level headings (up to the sixth) for the sections; in the single HTML file they appear in the table of contents of the page. Objects become bullet lists and arrays of objects become numbered lists; when every object has the same plain fields in the same order they become a table. Empty values create no section.

The file `docs/out/_tree.md` shows the documents nested by parent, starting with the roots. Pages with the same parent, and the pages without a parent, are sorted by `order`, and the pages without it come after the rest, sorted by title: ignoring case, numbers by value, Latin before Cyrillic, with the same rules on every machine; equal titles go by id.

With `"numbering": true` in `docc.json` docc numbers the pages: the children of the roots get 1, 2 and so on, deeper pages 2.1, and the sections of a field 2.1.1. The numbers appear in headings, in the tree, in the navigation and in the text of links; anchors do not change. Hidden documents are left out of the count, so the audit build shows the same numbers. A number typed into a title or a section key is reported as DOC314.

`"lang": "ru"` in `docc.json` translates the fixed labels of the pages and of the single HTML file, such as Parent, Referenced by and Covered by; the default is English.

An image `![alt](path)` with a relative path is resolved from the folder of the document, checked by DOC213 and copied into the output folder at the same path as in the sources; the single HTML file embeds it as a data URI. Markdown footnotes are rendered in the HTML file.

The flags single and html of docc build also write all pages into one file next to the folder: docs/out.md and docs/out.html. The pages follow the order of the tree, and links between them are anchors inside the file, so the file works on its own. The Markdown file starts with the tree and puts an invisible anchor before every page and field section.

The HTML file is a single-page application that needs no network: Preact with htm (about 13 kB, embedded, no build step), the styles and a JSON island with the pages are inside. docc renders the Markdown of every block to HTML; the script draws one page at a time in one of two modes chosen in the header, Reading and Work (with the number of edits); the choice is kept in the browser and the first visit opens Reading with a one-line hint about the edits. Reading shows the final text only: the header, the document tree on the left with the headings of the current page under it, a search box, and the page with its breadcrumb trail, one-line fields collected into a property list, its child pages with the start of their text and the neighbours in tree order. Work adds the badges for kind, status, priority and tags, the related pages, the edits, the comments and the tools of a paragraph, and the left column gets the tabs Pages, Edits and Comments. Search finds paragraphs, says how many, and opens the page at the paragraph; the keys / and Ctrl+K open it. The address `#<id>/<JSON Pointer>` opens a page at a paragraph, an unknown address says that nothing is found there, and Back returns to the place of reading. In the tree, titles of pages of one level line up and the fold arrow sits in its own strip on the left. The tree starts folded and opens only the way to the current page; long lists show a window of items with buttons for the rest, so a thousand documents stay usable. The left column is docked from 1280 px and slides in as a modal panel on narrower screens; on a touch screen and below 820 px every control is at least 44 px. The menu ⋯ holds the overview of edits, the starting point, the page and paragraph history, the downloads, printing and the comment actions; ? opens the colours and the keys. With `"lang": "ru"` the usual statuses are translated on the badges. The theme follows the system; print gives the current page. Without scripts the file shows a note. Raw HTML written in the documents is dropped, only the line break in table cells is kept. The look is fixed, there are no templates; the only change is the branding below.

A block is one element of a document: a string of an array of strings, or the whole value of another field or section (a table or a list is one block). It is addressed by the document id and the JSON Pointer of the element, such as `/body/2`. In the Work mode the paragraph tools hold a comment and the history of the block, read from Git at build time: every version that changed its text with the date and the changed words, shown as plain text without Markdown marks; the uncommitted state of the working tree is the last version. Inserting a paragraph does not move the history of its neighbours: the strings of an array are matched by equal text, then by similar text, and the pairs keep their order, so a paragraph removed in one place and one added in another stay a removal and an addition. The file is for the customer, so the default build leaves out the hidden fields (notes, docIgnore, hidden), the authors and messages of the commits and, with `changesSince` in `docc.json` (a Git revision of the version the reader last received), everything before that revision; the full build keeps it all. The edits start at `changesSince` by default; the menu ⋯ moves the starting point. In the Work mode the edits are drawn in the text like a Git or IDE diff: the words of the old version are matched with the words of the rendered paragraph, so links, lists and tables stay, added words are underlined on green and removed ones struck out on red; a rewrite (under 40% shared words) and a code block show the previous text folded above instead. A bar left of a paragraph marks it changed (blue) or added (green, with a plus); a removed paragraph stays folded at its old place. A navigator at the bottom walks through the edits of every page with a counter and a Viewed box (keys J and K, F7, V marks viewed and goes to the next unviewed), the current paragraph has a frame, and a strip at the right edge marks the edits of the page. Viewed marks are kept in the browser with a hash of the text, so a paragraph changed again becomes unviewed. The Edits tab lists the edits by page with the number left, and a start card sums them up by page. Page history lists the versions of the page with their changed, added and removed paragraphs. Outside a Git repository there is no history.

A comment is written in the Work mode as a card on the right margin that does not make its paragraph taller (under the paragraph on a narrow screen), on a block or on selected words: a selection shows the button Comment on the selection (on a touch screen in the bottom bar), the fragment is highlighted and kept with a few characters around it, and a card whose fragment is gone says so. It is typed or dictated: the button Dictate turns on the speech recognition of the browser and pressing it again stops it (Chrome and Edge send the sound to their speech service). The field From keeps the last name and can be changed, so a call can record comments of more than one person; a comment can be edited, and its deletion undone. Comments stay in the browser, marked not sent, and the browser asks before the page closes with unsent ones; the header shows how many are not sent, and the tab Comments copies them as text for a messenger, ending with a `docc-comments:` line the team imports, or downloads them as a JSON file; `docc comments import` takes either ([Commands](commands.md)). Comments of `docc.comments.json` appear on their blocks and in the tab with their status and the team's reply, internal ones are left out; a browser comment that is already there leaves the browser. The menu ⋯ downloads the current page as Markdown, all pages in one Markdown file or all pages as separate files in a zip archive, the same Markdown as in the output folder.

The `branding` section of `docc.json` dresses the HTML file for a company: `name` (required), `url`, `logo` (a path from the project root; png, jpg, jpeg, gif, svg or webp, embedded once in the file), `accent` (dark theme and header), `accentLight` (links on the light theme; it must read on white) and `header` (background of the header, default #1f1f1f). The logo and the name sit on a dark header at the top of the sidebar and in the mobile bar, so a light logo is expected. A footer at the end of every page shows the name and the site. On paper the header turns into the name above a line in the accent colour; no background is printed. Without the section the file does not change, and the Markdown output is never branded. The year is not in the footer, so the file does not go stale on the first of January. A missing or wrong logo, a colour that is not `#rgb` or `#rrggbb` and an unknown key are configuration errors (exit code 2).

The output is deterministic: stable sorting, no timestamps, line feeds only, UTF-8 without a byte order mark. Carriage returns and byte order marks in input files and in the output folder are normalized when reading and comparing.

The source format is in [Document model](document-model.md).

## Audit build

The flag full on build adds hidden documents, notes and suppressions as service sections, and wraps every include in comments that show where the inserted text starts and ends.
